title: God with us (Matthew 1:18–25)
hookLine: sleep on it, people say. Joseph had already decided, and then he slept
tomorrow: why would a king be afraid of a baby?

lines: A JUST MAN, MIND MADE UP.
cards: Sleep on it. People say it before a big text, a job offer, a breakup. Joseph had already decided.

He's promised to Mary, and she is expecting a child that isn't his. Matthew calls him "a just man," and his justice is gentle: he "was minded to put her away privily," to end it quietly, with no public shame.
Then, "while he thought on these things," he falls asleep, and the angel of the Lord comes to him in a dream. In this whole chapter, Joseph never says a word.

teach.h: FEAR NOT, THOU SON OF DAVID.
teach.b: The angel starts with yesterday's family tree: "Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."

Then Matthew reaches back to words of the prophet Isaiah: "they shall call his name Emmanuel, which being interpreted is, God with us." Matthew translates the Hebrew name on the spot. Not God above us.
With. In Christian belief, that's what happened in Jesus: God came near, and here he comes near in a worried house, at night.
Then Joseph's whole answer, without a speech: "Then Joseph being raised from sleep did as the angel of the Lord had bidden him, and took unto him his wife."
The name he gives the boy, Matthew says, is Jesus; Emmanuel is the prophet's word for him.
One to tell a friend tonight: Matthew closes the same frame on his last page, with Jesus saying, "lo, I am with you alway, even unto the end of the world."
God with us on the first page. I am with you on the last.

how: In the weeks before Christmas, some churches sing the Advent hymn O come, O come, Emmanuel, and some read Matthew 1:18–25 aloud.

games.q: a coworker you barely know just lost her dad. on the drive in, a thought: bring her lunch. now you're at your desk. what would Joseph's way look like?
o: bring the lunch today, quietly, without a big speech.
wait for a clearer sign that she'd actually want it.
plan the perfect card first, so it's all done right.
games.why: Joseph, raised from sleep, did as he was bidden: no speech, no bargaining, no second sign asked for. the nudge was enough.

practice: Let one quiet nudge surface: a call you keep meaning to make, an apology, a kindness you shelved. Name it, then name the one thing that keeps stopping you.
Then choose the first plain step, small enough to take today, the way Joseph rose and simply did it, and hold that step in mind as you breathe.

wordCard.voice: Emmanuel. A Hebrew name Matthew translates for us: God with us, on his first page, and kept to his last.

orig.note: Greek, carrying a Hebrew name: with us, God. Matthew 1:23 translates it right away: God with us.

carryVoice: Pocket this one: god with us, and a man who got up and lived it without a word. Week done.
